title: Jefferson for Adams and Jeanty: Philly Bets on One Name, Kai Takes the Points, and the Model Sends Both a Bill
dek: Alan swapped 126.4 points of production for Justin Jefferson's 38.4, and the model docked Team Pillbert five points of title odds while Mekhi's Dawgs lost just one.
body: Before Week 5, Alan's Team Pillbert sent wide receiver Davante Adams and running back Ashton Jeanty to Mekhi's Dawgs for wide receiver Justin Jefferson. It's a two-for-one between a 3-1 contender and a 1-3 team trying to climb back, and all three players spent all four weeks on a roster, so the sample is complete. The raw numbers are startling: Adams had 62 points and Jeanty had 64.4, a combined 126.4, while Jefferson had 38.4. Alan gave up more than three times the production he got back.

Start with Kai's haul, because it's the easiest to explain. Jeanty has averaged about 16.1 points a week, and Adams about 15.5, so Mekhi added two players who have each been outscoring Jefferson's 9.6-a-week pace by six points or more. For a team at 1-3 that just watched Ja'Marr Chase post 4.2, getting two steady weekly contributors is exactly the right medicine. Mekhi may know more football than anyone in this league, and this looks like the move of a guy who reads the box scores and likes what they say.

Alan's side requires a little faith. Phillibert is betting that Jefferson's first four weeks are the low point, not the trend, and that one elite receiver at his best is worth more than two very good players filling separate lineup slots. There's a real logic to consolidating talent on a contender, but this isn't a typical consolidation, since Jefferson scored less than either player Alan sent away. Jeanty also barely had time to learn where Team Pillbert keeps the snacks, arriving from Jordan and leaving for Mekhi within the same stretch of deals.

The model was not persuaded by Philly's vision. Team Pillbert's title odds fell from 21% to 16%, a 5-point drop, while Dawgs slipped from 4% to 3%, just 1 point. In proportional terms both teams lost roughly a quarter of their chances, but Mekhi paid one point of odds for 88 extra points of past production, and Alan paid five for the privilege of acquiring a lower scorer. On paper, Kai wins this one, and it isn't close.

The best part is that nobody has to wait for the verdict. Dawgs and Team Pillbert meet in Week 5, which means Adams and Jeanty face the team that shipped them out, and Jefferson debuts against his old manager. If Jefferson erupts and Alan moves to 4-1, he'll argue the model was reading the wrong numbers. If Adams and Jeanty combine for another 30-plus, Mekhi will have won the trade and the game in the same afternoon.

social.author: Dawgs Pound Supporters Club
social.text: We sent out 38.4 points. We got back 126.4. Then we checked the schedule and saw who we play Sunday. Christmas came early in Week 5.

social.author: Pillbert Faithful
social.text: Points before the trade don't score after the trade. You buy the star, you live with the star. Jefferson, welcome. Go remind your old team who you are.

social.author: Spreadsheet Steve
social.text: Weekly rates: Jeanty 16.1, Adams 15.5, Jefferson 9.6. Odds: Pillbert -5, Dawgs -1. I ran it three times and the math kept rooting for Kai.

social.author: The Buckaroo Insider
social.text: Ashton Jeanty has now been traded twice before Week 5. Somebody get that man a forwarding address and a team sweatshirt that fits.
